newsitem.title: USA: Duke shutting McGuire N.C. power plants.
newsitem.headline: Duke shutting McGuire N.C. power plants.

text.p: Duke Power Co has begun shutting down its McGuire 1 and 2 nuclear power stations because of problems with batteries at the facility, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported Thursday.
The two units are rated at 1,129 megawatts (MW) each.
The NRC, citing a plant status report from the operator, said Duke initiated the shutdown after a 125 volt battery bank failed to meet the criteria for a modified performance test.
The battery bank is shared by both units.
"The battery was declared inoperable on Oct 28 at 0956 EST and required to be operable or the plant will be (fully) shut down by Oct 31 at 0956 EST," the NRC said.
Unit 1 is being brought down first, at a rate of 20 percent an hour, followed by unit 2.
No estimate was given for when the units might be restarted and company officials were not immediately available for comment.
The McGuire power plant is in Cornelius, N.C.
Duke Power Co, based in Charlotte, N.C., has an overall generation capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which about 12 percent comes from the McGuire facility.
